info.name: Paiflow API v1
info.description:
Execute a deployed deposit-triggered flow and poll its events. Fill in the collection variables `deploymentId`, `apiToken` (minted by the deployment's owner in the API access panel), `from` and `amount`.

The API never signs. Run **Prepare execute**, sign the `unsignedXdr` variable it stores with the `from` key on your side (`stellar tx sign --sign-with-key S… --network testnet`), paste the result into `signedXdr`, then run **Submit execute**. Guide: docs/api/README.md in the repository.

request.description:
Public; no token and no account. Returns a bearer token for one shared swapper deployment on testnet, so you can run the calls above before registering. Takes no body. Available only where the public demo is enabled (the testnet instance); 403 otherwise.

**This deployment is shared.** Anyone else holding a demo token can read the events your deposit produces, including the account you deposited from. The swap proceeds are paid to a Paiflow-owned testnet account, not back to you, so the testnet XLM you deposit is spent. Fund a throwaway account with friendbot and never point this at an account you care about.

For an isolated deployment and a token that does not expire in an hour, register, deploy your own flow and mint a token in the **API access** panel.

Rate limit: 3 requests per 3600 seconds per client IP. Rate limit: 60 requests per 3600 seconds instance-wide.
Discover recorded integration support and prerequisites. Requires the deployment token. Conditional support is not live eligibility; no transactions are sent.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Public; no token. Returned as the bare document, without the `data` envelope. Rate limit: 60 requests per 60 seconds per client IP.

Prepare the deposit that executes a deposit-triggered flow. `from` must be a funded account on this network: it pays the deposit and the fee, and signs the envelope. The flow's payout recipient must hold a trustline for the asset it receives; a missing trustline reverts the whole pipeline.

The flow runs through its deposit trigger; the next pipeline steps (pay, split, condition, swap) run in the same transaction. Sign the returned `xdr` with the `from` key using `networkPassphrase`, before `expiresAt`, and post it to `execute/submit`. Only flows that start with a deposit trigger can be executed; subscription, webhook, payroll and other trigger-headed flows are refused with `VALIDATION`.

Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds per token.

The collection saves executeUnsignedXdr and its preparation ID. Sign this envelope and paste the result into executeSignedXdr. A successful new preparation replaces this operation's unsigned envelope and ID and clears its previous signed envelope. Failed preparations preserve the previous payment's retry data.

response.name: 401 Unauthorized
422 Validation

request.description:
Submit a signed deposit that executes a deposit-triggered flow.

The envelope must be the one `execute` returned, signed by `from`: anything but a single `deposit` call on this flow's trigger contract is refused with `VALIDATION`, as is a fee-bump envelope.

Idempotent on the envelope hash: submitting the same `signedXdr` again never sends a second transaction, it reports the one already on the network. That is also how to check a `PENDING` result. A transaction that reached the network and failed is a `200` with `status: FAILED` and an `error`, not an HTTP error.

Rate limit: 30 requests per 60 seconds per token.

The collection sends the matching preparation response ID as x-preparation-request-id when available. Reuse it for retries of this envelope; a new prepare replaces its own operation ID. It is optional analytics metadata, not payment authorization.

response.name: 200 FAILED

request.description: Release a timelock branch's before side now (work delivered). Omit `nodeId` when the deployment has one timelock branch. Rate limit: 10 requests per 60 seconds per token.

request.description:
Forward-paginated events the app decoded for this deployment's contracts, ascending by `(ledger, eventId)`. This is the app's record, not a raw chain feed: each event appears once (`eventId` is unique).

**Freshness.** When this deployment's events were last collected from the network more than 10 seconds ago, a call collects them first and waits up to 5 seconds for that before answering from the record. So an event usually appears within 10 to 20 seconds of its ledger closing, whoever submitted the transaction (a wallet paying the contract directly, a scanned SEP-7 QR, a scheduled charge), provided you keep polling. Collection is shared by every caller of the deployment: one at a time, and the next no sooner than 10 seconds after the last one ends, so polling faster than that does not make events arrive sooner. A call that arrives while a collection is already running, or when the network is slow, answers with what is recorded, and the event appears on a later call; a background poller also collects every minute. A confirmed `execute/submit` records its own events before it returns.

A swap is `kind: PAYOUT` with `topic: "swap"` and `data` `{ assetIn, assetOut, amountIn, amountOut }`; amounts are stroops as strings.

To poll: store `nextCursor` and pass it back as `cursor`. While `hasMore` is true, ask again straight away; once it is false, wait and ask again with the same cursor. `nextCursor` is never null once the deployment has events: on an empty page it echoes the cursor you sent. It is null only when there are no events and no cursor was sent.

Rate limit: 120 requests per 60 seconds per token.

request.description:
Configure one immediate PAYER_DEV recipient and prepare its deposit. Requires functioning Redis. Fixed Split is accepted only with empty balances and immediate surplus forwarding. Fill via API uses 100%; configured values must leave no funds in Pay. Sign xdr and submit it with the same token to payouts/submit. Direct deposits, execute, owner transactions and legacy mutations bypass coordination. Payout deposits expire after 60 seconds; execute keeps 180 seconds. Sign and submit before expiresAt. A 409 includes Retry-After when a held transaction is known: seconds until maxTime, rounded up (minimum 1). It is advisory; ledger-time expiry or finality is still required and a retry may return 409 again.

The collection saves payoutUnsignedXdr and its preparation ID. Sign this envelope and paste the result into payoutSignedXdr. A successful new preparation replaces this operation's unsigned envelope and ID and clears its previous signed envelope. Failed preparations preserve the previous payment's retry data.

request.description:
Only the exact prepared deposit for this deployment and token is accepted, with envelope signatures added. Retry the same signedXdr on PENDING. Protection remains through uncertain outcomes and can only be replaced after finality or ledger-time expiry. Final retries cannot release newer holders.

The collection sends the matching preparation response ID as x-preparation-request-id when available. Reuse it for retries of this envelope; a new prepare replaces its own operation ID. It is optional analytics metadata, not payment authorization.

request.description: Poll existing transaction without resubmitting; UNKNOWN never authorizes another payment.

Requires a separately funded webhook deployment and its callback secret. Keep the same event key and payload for retries; changing payload conflicts. Keys never reopen automatically; UNKNOWN must not trigger a fresh payment. This route uses the relayer, not caller wallet signing.
Read live subscriber, token, allowance and cancellation state. Unconfigured Dev subscriber returns setupRequired:true and allowance:"0". Read only; no wallet mutation. Limit 40/minute/token.
